claims.text: ResetAsync runs `TRUNCATE customers, products, orders, order_items, payments, notifications CASCADE` through ExecuteSqlRawAsync on a new context.

TRUNCATE removes all rows, keeping tables; CASCADE also truncates tables with FK references to a listed table (none extra here: all six listed); without RESTART IDENTITY (default CONTINUE IDENTITY) sequences are not reset.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: SQL Commands > TRUNCATE (RESTART IDENTITY, CONTINUE IDENTITY, CASCADE)

claims.text: Resetting at the start of each test means rows left by a test that stopped halfway (failed assertion, exception, a run stopped from outside) cannot reach the next test; clean-up at the end of a test body would be skipped.

Because sequences keep counting after TRUNCATE, a test cannot assume its first order gets id 1; EfOrderRepositoryTests uses the ids returned by its own inserts (InsertCustomerAndProductsAsync, order.Id after save).

EfOrderRepositoryTests.DisposeAsync does nothing; OrdersApiTests resets its own database the same way; ResetAsync uses CreateContext() and ExecuteSqlRawAsync; the TRUNCATE list does not include __EFMigrationsHistory.
One container serves the whole test class, so its database keeps rows across the class's tests until something empties it.

In a stage-2 checkout with `database.ResetAsync()` replaced by `Task.CompletedTask`: the EfOrderRepositoryTests filter fails 1 (SaveChangesAsync_OrderForMissingCustomer_IsRefused, 23505 IX_customers_email), passes 1; that test alone passes.
claims.source_hint: verified by execution, two runs, same result (scratchpad it-a/evidence-tc.txt)

claims.text: xUnit creates a new instance of the test class for every test it runs, so a test class's IAsyncLifetime.InitializeAsync runs before every test.
